text:
Marathon Petroleum climbed 1.95% today to $418.84, continuing a strong two-week rally that's now up 9.4%. The move follows a report that a damaged Saudi pipeline will restart operations within days, which eased immediate concerns about oil supply disruption—crude prices fell on the news, and U.S. oil is trading at $97.26 per barrel. With U.S. refineries running at 97.8% capacity and diesel hitting an all-time high of $6.31 per gallon, refiners like Marathon are benefiting from tight fuel supply and high refining margins (the profit spread between crude input and finished fuel output).

The broader context is a refining environment caught between rising fuel demand and constrained supply. While geopolitical tensions in the Middle East had threatened to tighten oil markets further, the Saudi pipeline restart reduces that immediate risk—but diesel scarcity remains acute, keeping pressure on prices and refiners' profitability high.
